author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction changes that visit in place, never adds another visit to the pet, and returns to the owner's record. The correction is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the visit form shows that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when its correction supplies a description and a date later than today, then that visit carries both and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has the same number of visits as before
given a correction with a blank description, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the visit is unchanged
given a correction with a date of today or earlier, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the visit is unchanged
edge case 3: correcting a visit is refused when the visit does not exist, the visit belongs to another pet, or the pet does not belong to the named owner
edge case 4: a visit whose date has passed cannot keep that date; its correction is refused unless the date moves later than today
non_goals: any link or entry point to the correction from the owner's record or any other page (owner decision, intake line 1: reachable by its URL alone; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
changing anything about a visit other than its date and description, including moving it to another pet
new user-facing wording: no correction-specific confirmation message and no new submit label; either would fall under REQ-LANG-002 and need every supported language
notes: Owner-stated scope, intake line 1 (source: task-prompt). The request fixes the URL (GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit), the reused template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, and its `visit` model attribute. Those are owner constraints passed to design, not PRD content. Validation matches booking (REQ-VIS-001): description required, date later than today. Success redirects to the owner detail page; failure redisplays the form. Decided here as reversible, narrowest readings: (a) edge case 3 refuses a visit/pet/owner mismatch, the same way booking's edge case 1 does; (b) a refused correction leaves the visit unchanged; (c) no confirmation message is required on success. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: (1) whether a past-dated visit should be correctable without moving its date (today it cannot be, edge case 4); (2) how staff reach the correction, and the kept booking submit label. Durable writes this dispatch: the docs/prd.md NG-5 row, preamble, Visits section, and Open Questions; the new docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the status line of docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. Needs its owner: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the 2026-09-12 non-goal ADR, and that file is outside the product expert's write scope. Design context: the current visit model attribute always appends a fresh visit to the pet, and the no-additional-visit criterion targets exactly that. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction follows the existing owner-aggregate write path (system-design.md Contracts: OwnerRepository is the sole write path; Pet and Visit persist only by cascade from Owner). It also follows the adjacent pet-edit seam, where PetController.findPet takes an optional petId path variable and resolves the existing child through Owner.getPet. The small adjustment is that VisitController's `visit` model attribute resolves an existing visit by identity through a new Pet.getVisit(Integer) when the route names a visitId. Only the booking route keeps appending a fresh visit. Basis: grep and Read of VisitController.java, PetController.java, Owner.java:126, and Pet.java. The IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker basis. Contracts rows now carry REQ-VIS-003 on Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController.
integration_points: Model attribute: loadPetWithVisit gains `@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId`, as PetController.findPet does for petId. With a visitId it returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and throws IllegalArgumentException on null, like the existing owner and pet lookups (booking edge case 1's refusal). Without a visitId it appends a fresh visit exactly as today, leaving booking unchanged.

Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id): it searches only this pet's persisted visits. A visit belonging to another pet therefore resolves to null. With the existing pet-of-owner check, one null check covers all of edge case 3.
Binding, GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: binds nothing from the request; path variables only.

Binding, POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: the target is the persisted Visit resolved through the owner aggregate, behind an allow-list of `date` and `description` (`@InitBinder("visit")` with setAllowedFields). The class-wide id disallow stays (security-principles.md Realization, mass-assignment row). The allow-list also governs booking's `visit` attribute with no behaviour change, because the booking form offers only those two fields.

Owner in the correction handler: take it as `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) Owner owner`. Never bind request parameters onto it, and do not copy the booking handler's signature (system-design.md Known Defects, owner-binding row).

Date rule: extract the booking handler's inline non-future-date check into one private VisitController method that both handlers call (system-design.md VisitController row). Edge case 4 follows from the same check with no extra rule.

Outcome: on success, owners.save(owner) then redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with no flash message; the PRD non-goal bars new correction wording under REQ-LANG-002. On a field error, redisplay pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm before any save.
Template: no change expected. The form has no th:action, so it posts to its own address. The header drops `New` for a persisted visit, and the booking submit label stays per the PRD non-goal.

Double, repository boundary: VisitControllerTests keeps its existing `@MockitoBean OwnerRepository` as a conscious framework stub. A hand-written double does not fit because OwnerRepository extends the wide JpaRepository interface. A real repository does not fit because @WebMvcTest excludes JPA. Assert persistence on the Owner passed to save: capture it, then check the same visit count and that the visit carries the new date and description. On refusal, assert save is never invoked. The fixture pet gains one persisted visit with its id set.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned harness). A lookup refusal escapes perform() as a ServletException caused by IllegalArgumentException; assert that cause.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: the correction binds only the visit's date and description. VisitController adds `@InitBinder("visit")` with `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description")` alongside the existing `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")`, and the owner is taken with `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, so a crafted `lastName` or `id` cannot reach the saved aggregate. This is stronger than the baseline, and the allow-list also narrows the booking path's visit binding. Covered by VisitControllerTests `theVisitCorrectionShouldNotChangeTheOwnerFromRequestParameters`.

Ownership chain and cross-request state: each correction request re-resolves owner, then pet, then visit from the path. `owners.findById(ownerId)` then `owner.getPet(petId)` then `pet.getVisit(visitId)`, and the new `Pet.getVisit` matches only persisted visits in that pet's own collection (`!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)`). A visit of another pet or owner is unreachable, which satisfies the brief's 'Trusting cross-request state' row. The visit id is never bound from the request.

Validation parity: the correction handler carries `@Valid Visit` (Visit.description is `@NotBlank`) and reuses the extracted `rejectDateNotLaterThanToday` shared with booking, so every path that persists a visit enforces the same rules. A refused correction returns before `this.owners.save(owner)`. With `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties) the loaded entities are detached, so the in-memory binding onto a refused visit is never flushed.

Error surface: the new not-found IllegalArgumentException message carries only the three route identifiers, which are typed `int`/`Integer` path variables and so cannot carry markup or secrets. The message matches the existing owner and pet not-found messages in the same method.

Output escaping: the form template is unchanged and renders visit and owner values through `th:text`/`th:field`. A grep of the added lines for `utext` and `__${` returned 0 matches, so no escaping was disabled and no template preprocessing was added.

Detection sweep over the diff's added lines (`grep -F -c` on the `scripts/changeset.sh` '+' lines) returned 0 for Runtime, ProcessBuilder, exec(, JsonTypeInfo, enableDefaultTyping, Files., FileWriter, /tmp/, createQuery, nativeQuery, System.out, password, secret, token and key=. That rules out new shell execution, unsafe deserialization, file I/O, hand-built queries and committed credentials. No new logging was added.

Exposed surface: the change adds two unauthenticated routes, GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. They follow the documented demonstration baseline (no authn, authz or CSRF, per system-design.md Security Context) and do not widen it. No actuator exposure or configuration was changed.

Supply chain: build.gradle and pom.xml are unchanged (`git diff HEAD --stat` empty), so no dependency was added. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson), Thymeleaf 3.1.5, Hibernate 7.4.5.Final.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit's date and description

blast_radius.note: Two production files in the owner package (VisitController, Pet), one module, 84 prod lines; the rest of the 39 hunks are tests and docs. The shared loadPetWithVisit model attribute and the new @InitBinder("visit") allow-list also govern booking, but booking keeps its fresh-visit branch when visitId is null and its existing tests still pass, so the reach stays contained despite VisitController being a declared security surface.

semantic_surprise.note: A correction can erase a booked visit's date: an empty date param binds to null, rejectDateNotLaterThanToday skips null, Visit.date carries no @NotNull, visit_date is nullable in all three schemas, and the date input (fragments/inputField.html:14) has no required attribute, so clearing the field in the browser saves the visit with no date. Booking has the same gap, but on a correction it overwrites stored data rather than creating a dateless new visit. Two smaller points: on a refused correction the form's previous-visits table (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:51) lists the rejected, unsaved values for the visit being corrected, because binding mutated the in-memory visit; and by design a past visit's description can never be fixed without moving its date forward (recorded as a PRD open question).

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes: the saved Owner is captured and the named visit's date and description are checked, the pet's visit count is unchanged, save is never called on blank-description, today, or kept-past-date refusals, a tampered lastName does not reach the owner, and three ownership mismatches throw; PetTests covers Pet.getVisit at the unit seam. The today/tomorrow boundary is covered. Gaps: no empty-date correction test, and the claim that a refused visit is unchanged rests on save never being called, which is sound only because open-in-view=false (application.properties:11) and cannot be exercised in the WebMvc slice.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers on the first-pass full battery approved with cited evidence, apart from one doc-reviewer autofix (colon vs em-dash in the new ADR). The fix-delta roster (code-quality, doc) re-approved it cleanly. Spot-checked citations resolve: Owner.java:121-136 getPet, VisitControllerTests.java:188-198 tamper test, open-in-view=false. The OWASP-not-configured note restates a standing project gap. Nobody raised the null-date path, but that is a miss, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions; the second design-block was a punctuation-only fix dispatch.
